newsitem.title: USA: Sprint Q4 long-distance revenues rise.
newsitem.headline: Sprint Q4 long-distance revenues rise.

text.p: Sprint Corp said Tuesday its long-distance division recorded a 12.3 percent rise in revenues to $2.16 billion in the fourth quarter, and long-distance operating income rose 27.4 percent to $257 million.
Local telephone revenues were up 7.9 percent to $1.33 billion, and operating income rose 12.4 percent to $334 million.
Access lines increased by 5.6 percent to more than 7.1 million in the quarter, Sprint added.

"Nearly one-third of the access lines we added in the quarter were for second-line service to existing customers to meet their lifestyle and data access needs," William Esrey, Sprint chairman, said in a statement. "Overall, more than nine percent of our customres now have second lines into their homes."
Commenting on long-distance operations, Esrey said the consumer, business and wholesale segments each recorded double-digit growth in revenues and call volume.
He added that, despite a fiercely competitive marketplace, Sprint grew its market share in long distance profitably.

Earlier, Sprint reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.57 a share compared with a loss of $0.98, both after charges. Operating income from continuing operations, before charges and ventures, rose to $347.0 million from $290.0 million.
